stem: A crop repeatedly reaches severe wilt before each irrigation and then recovers after watering. Which strategy is strongest?
choices: Continue using visible wilt as the irrigation trigger because rapid recovery shows the timing is appropriate
Increase root-zone EC so plants retain more internal water and tolerate the existing dryback interval better
Extend the dryback interval further so repeated recovery strengthens roots and improves future drought tolerance
Set irrigation from measured depletion and crop response so dryback stays adequate without repeated severe wilt
rationale: Repeated severe wilt indicates the dryback target is too aggressive. Irrigation should use measured root-zone depletion and crop response to balance aeration with avoidance of excessive water stress.
